A moderate-paced start was made with Green, Rickards and Bentley in the lead, closely followed by Martin, Tookey, Bidgood and Harley. Before two miles had been covered, Martin had joined the leaders and in this order they proceeded along Parkside towards "The Green Man" Roehampton.
Fred Rickards was always with the leaders, and overcoming a slight feeling of weakness at 16 miles, completed the course in second position, and stronger than anyone.
An account of the "National" appears elsewhere in this issue, but it would not be out of place here to mention again the very fine form shown by one of the best of sportsmen, Fred Rickards.
A Belgrave team went to Birmingham on July 14th to compete in Lewis's 25 miles walk, but with Green an absentee and Rickards barely recovered from a very severe chill, we were not too strong.
Over this stretch of 31 miles odd, Lloyd Johnson (Leicester), Whitlock (Metropolitan W.C.) and our own warrior, Fred Rickards, had a great battle.

With the New Year, we shall see them back in harness again, preparing for the 20 miles Championship, which has eluded us in recent years, despite some really fine walking on the part of our men. Bentley, Rickards, Bidgood, Martin, J.

From the start Jack Field cut out the pace, opening up a distance of 50 yards in the first mile from Bentley, Bidgood, Harley, Martin, Speechley and Rickards, all of whom appeared unconcerned at the pace set by the leader.

A little farther back were Bentley, Bidgood, Rickards and Joe King, all walking together. It was as early as this that Jock Martin was having a struggle, suffering from a touch of sunstroke, but manfully keeping going.
Despite the absence of Tommy Green, who was nursing some slight strains, we had every reason to feel confident of success, for we had last year's winning team and, in addition, Fred Rickards.

Tommy Green was the first to reach the finishing post, closely followed by Fred Rickards. Fred, who was winning this race years ago, seems fitter than ever, and we may confidently expect him to demand the attention of the selectors when our Olympic athletes are chosen.
We have held the team title for the last two years; and with Green, Rickards and Bentley, all Olympic possibilities, supported by others, we should claim a "hat trick."

Bentley, with three toenails missing, was an enforced absentee, as were also Green and Rickards. In fact, six only of our men entered, and we must look to it that next year's race will find more of our walkers with the inclination to essay the Brighton course.

Churcher, Fletcher, Green, Harley, Readman and Rickards, should be our team. Unfortunately, Fletcher was indisposed, Green was unable to turn out, and Rickards was also compelled to stand down at the last moment.
Fred Rickards was having a bad time, and had dropped back a little. Jack Bidgood and Colin Sutton were walking well together for our third scoring position.
Bentley and Rickards were among those who retired, but we are always assured of a first-rate performance from these two loyal team men when the National Championship comes along.
